readings.title: The rehearsal from the doorway
readings.instruction: Read the original passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: Organisers rehearsed their welcome talk from the stage and thought the event was ready. A volunteer then walked in from the street as a first-time visitor. She found no sign at the side entrance and could not tell which desk handled registration. Two simple arrows and a clearly labelled table solved the problem. The rehearsal had improved when it began where the audience's experience began, rather than where the organisers usually stood.
knowledgePoints: 阅读理解：主旨、细节、推断与词义

readings.title: The talk without the slides
readings.instruction: Read the original passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: A projector stopped working just before a local history talk. The speaker had brought a one-page outline and three printed photographs because the venue had warned that equipment could be unreliable. She used these materials and invited more questions between sections. The talk differed from her plan but still covered its main purpose. Afterwards, she noted which images genuinely needed projection and which had only repeated words she could easily explain.

readings.title: The form after the applause
readings.instruction: Read the original passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: A community workshop received many feedback forms marked 'excellent', but organisers did not know which features to repeat. At the next workshop they asked visitors to name one useful activity and one confusing moment. Fewer forms contained only a tick, and several comments identified an instruction that needed rewriting. Satisfaction remained worth knowing, but more specific questions produced information the organisers could act on. They reported the resulting change at the following session.

readings.title: The contact list that fitted a pocket
readings.instruction: Read the original passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: A volunteer event relied on a long planning document kept in the coordinator's bag. When a delivery arrived at the wrong entrance, helpers did not know whom to call. For the next event, the coordinator gave each team a small card with roles, contact numbers and the agreed meeting point. Detailed plans remained available separately. The card did not replace planning; it made the most urgent information easy to find at the moment someone needed it.

translation.stem:
Translate this original passage into natural Chinese, preserving its meaning and logical connections.

Preparing an event means thinking about the moments when the original plan may no longer work. A short outline, a clear contact list or a spare activity can keep a small problem from interrupting the whole programme. These preparations are most useful when everyone knows where to find them. A backup that nobody can locate offers little practical help.
translation.referenceAnswer: 筹备活动意味着考虑原计划可能无法继续执行的时刻。简短提纲、清晰的联系人名单或备用活动，可以防止小问题打断整个流程。当每个人都知道去哪里找到这些准备材料时，它们最有用。无人能找到的备用方案，在实际中帮助很小。
translation.explanation: 参考译文不是唯一答案；信息完整、逻辑准确且中文自然的其他译法同样有效。

writing.stem:
Write about 120 words in English for this original simulation task.

You are organising a community learning event. Write a message to volunteers explaining the arrival procedure, one backup arrangement, and how useful feedback will be collected.
writing.sampleAnswer: Dear Volunteers, Thank you for helping with Saturday's learning event. Please arrive at nine and meet at the registration table beside the main entrance. Each team will receive a card showing its role and the coordinator's contact number. Walk the visitor route once before the doors open so that missing signs can be corrected. If the guest speaker is delayed, we will begin with the prepared small-group activity; the host will announce the change. At the end, please invite visitors to name one useful activity and one point that was unclear on the feedback form. Names are optional. We will discuss these comments together next week and record one practical improvement for our next event. Best wishes, The Organising Team.
writing.explanation: 范文展示一种可行的回应；允许不同观点和例子，按任务完成、组织和语言评分。

criteria.name: 任务完成与内容
criteria.description: 回应题目全部要求，观点明确，理由、例子或建议与情境相关。

criteria.name: 组织与衔接
criteria.description: 段落信息顺序合理，衔接自然，格式适合写作目的。

criteria.name: 语言与表达
criteria.description: 用词恰当，语法准确；按错误对理解的影响扣分。

knowledgePoints: 英语写作：任务回应与连贯表达
